title: What Do British People Complain About Most?
paragraphs: What annoys you most when you're out in public? People being rude? Someone pushing ahead of you in a line? Or perhaps someone using their phone's speaker in public?
A new survey shows that British people have a lot to complain about.
The survey, done by YouGov, asked more than 2,000 people across the UK what bothers them about other people when they're in public.
The biggest complaint was people being rude to shop and restaurant workers, which annoys 67% of people who took the survey. People who don't wait their turn in a line came second, at 59%.
Other common problems included people using their phone speakers in public, people taking up too much space on streets or buses and trains, and people making videos of themselves for social media.
But while these things bother people, they aren't actually the things they complain about most.
In fact, when asked what they complain about most in everyday life, 24% chose things they see in the news. Another 18% chose people being rude — so that's on both lists — while 11% chose work.
And although British people are famous for talking about the country's bad weather, only 6% said the weather was what they complain about most. And just 8% chose traffic.
Overall, 76% said they were people who often complain, while 20% said they never do.
And of the complainers, almost half said they usually share their problems with family or a partner, instead of speaking to the person who upset them.
